correctness.rationale: The all-positive trace and transitivity force each triple to contribute at most two support edges; supports of size ≥2m-1 have a forced-negative contradiction. The explicit m-1 path-plus-reserve construction realizes all labels on 2m-2 edges. A complete depth-2m decision tree is impossible because 2m-1 successive positive branching edges determine a unique partition. A separate m-2 path plus two one-edge units support has at least two realizing partitions for every label, yielding a depth-(2m-1) tree. Every case including m=1 and r=1/r=2 derangements is handled. CHECK.py exhaustively corroborates n=3,6,9 static ranks and n=6,9 online ranks.

originality.rationale: Bressan et al. (arXiv:1905.11902), Theorem 6, prove VC dimension n-1 for ALL set partitions, not partitions with every block of size 3 and not the sharp online dimension 2m-1. Liu–Mukherjee (arXiv:2112.07897) prove an identification-query bound for partitions into k components, with arbitrary component sizes. Guingona et al. (arXiv:2109.04805) prove VC/Littlestone equality for linear zero sets, not this concept class. No stronger implication covering the present all-order uniform-triple exact gap was found. Searches are not proof of global priority; alternate terminology is residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier result under the name uniform equivalence relations, triple factors, or three-uniform set partitions might be undiscovered; negative searches do not certify priority.
Full text of Guingona et al. and semi-random-noise clustering paper was not examined, although their stated theorem models differ.

value.rationale: The all-order exact strict gap is a natural invariant of balanced three-way cluster membership constraints. Unlike the unrestricted equivalence-relation concept class, limiting block sizes creates a persistent adaptive advantage; the strong-trace two-witness construction explains it and is reusable. The theorem is a motivated infinite family, not a special small enumeration or a cosmetic rephrasing of ordinary forests. Scope excludes other block sizes and noisy/reconstruction-query models.
